Two parts of the round-0 change are still unwritten, both in scope's text. (a) §7.7's fixtures cite '§13.2's T20 group' (l.11383), but §13.2's T20 group (l.16666-16679) lists none of them. They have no id and no §13.8 tier row, so no CI tier runs them. (b) Part A still records the unlimited rule. J-DET-11 (rationale l.111, R25 l.1886) reads 'a host that must override a lock sends an unlock first', and J-A20.71 (rationale l.327) reads 'J-DET-11 already makes a host unlock before it overrides a lock'. Both contradict §7.7. Determinism-r1t's VDC1-17 and VDC1-19 report the same remaining defect.

(T20-14) A dossier rename on a locked name path, and a `ruined` and a `removed` state on an institution whose building is locked: each lands, the lock is reported orphaned in the event's disruption report, and every other locked entity is byte-identical. J-A20.71 (l.327) reads '… while J-DET-11 makes a host's map event unlock before it overrides a lock, a dossier event superseding the locks on what it changes (§7.7)'.

issues.claim: A repair this round created a new conflict at an edge. The VEL0-01 fix (§7.7's precedence, l.11379-11382) lets a dossier population fall empty a locked or pinned dwelling by a `relet` down: 'even a protected dwelling's last household, its building then standing empty but never `vacate`d, so it keeps its state, shell, existence and every locked path'. §2.6's one statement of the clamp (l.2110-2111) says 'a residential building's `households` count lies in [1, capacity]' and that 'the bound holds through every change'; §4.11's `relet` reads that clamp. The edge now has two outcomes. Under §7.7, a building that is not vacant holds 0 households, which §2.6 forbids. Under §2.6, the clamp keeps 1 household, so the dossier's population is not met, against item 8 (f) and §7.7. No text defines how the readers of `Building.households` treat a non-vacant residential building with no household. Those readers are S11's fill, F-PLAN and the plan rung, V06's ledger and departures, and §10.3.
issues.required_change: §2.6's clamp (l.2110-2111) reads: 'a residential building's `households` count lies in [1, capacity] — 0 only for a `vacant` building (§4.11's `vacate`) and for a locked or pinned dwelling a dossier population fall has emptied (§7.7's precedence), which keeps its occupancy state, shell and every locked path and is let again by regrowth's `relet` up like any standing shell — and a non-residential building's is 0'. F-PLAN and the plan rung read that case as a vacant shell's plan (no unit housed), and the generation fill never produces it. §5.3's capacity row gains the lower bound with the same exception.

issues.claim: A repair this round created a new conflict at an edge. §4.11's epoch step (c) (l.7804-7806) says 'a building whose household count falls but not to zero takes a `relet` down … and `vacate` fires only when its last household leaves'. The strike pool (l.8262-8263) says 'a `relet` down while households remain, `vacate` at a building's last household (J-A28.45)'. Neither has an exception, and §4.11's `LadderOp` `relet` (l.7860) bounds its `households` 'within §2.6's capacity', which §2.6 clamps to [1, capacity]. The VEL0-01 fix in §7.7's precedence (l.11379-11382) says a locked or pinned dwelling's last household leaves under a dossier fall by a `relet` down, and the building is 'never `vacate`d'. An epoch that follows §4.11 vacates a locked building and so changes a locked state, which §7.7 forbids. An epoch that follows §7.7 emits a `relet` to 0, which `LadderOp` does not admit.

issues.claim: Item 123 (J136) assigns determinism '§6.3 (one keyed threshold per plan element by lineage and element id; no new ids; monotone in the decay level)'. §6.3 has no such rule: 'item 123', 'damage layer' and 'decay level' appear 0 times in the base, and §6.1 registers no concern for it.
issues.required_change: §6.3 gains the damage thresholds. Each plan element (each wall run, floor area, door, window, stair, roof bay over a room, furniture piece) draws one threshold in [0, 1) on a registered concern (§6.1, e.g. `plan.damage`, non-rerollable). The draw is keyed by the building's lineage and the element's id, at epoch component 0. No new id is minted, and every room, wall and opening id is unchanged. An element shows as damaged exactly when the building's decay level is at or above its threshold. Damage is therefore monotone (a higher level's damage contains a lower level's), stays in place, and leaves in reverse order as the level falls. §6.5 (9) gains a test that the same element breaks at the same level for a given seed on every engine.
